research_rationale: Read the complete held American Presidency Project transcription of Executive Order 6204-A (July 14, 1933). It approves only Section V, paragraphs (a), (b), (d) and (e) of the proposed Rayon Weaving code, effective July 17, 1933, "subject to the interpretations and conditions imposed by me on my approval of the corresponding provisions of said Cotton Textile Code" and to revision after a hearing set for July 25, 1933. Held Executive Order 6206-A (July 16, 1933) recites that the July 9, 1933 Cotton Textile approval contained "condition 12 of said order providing for the termination of approval at the end of four months unless expressly renewed" and withdraws that condition for the Cotton Textile code. Whether the imported conditions included a four-month termination of this partial approval, whether the July 16 withdrawal reached it, and whether a renewal, revision or later code replaced it before June 14, 1935 cannot be settled from held sources, so the first end is not established and no claim is submitted.

The recital states that an application was made for approval of the amendment of certain provisions of the code and that the order acts "in order to carry out the recommendations of the Board of Inquiry for the Cotton Textile Industry, created by Executive Order No. 6840, dated September 5, 1934, embodied in the report of said Board submitted to me September 17, 1934"; it recites no hearing and no report or findings of the Administrator. The held text does not reproduce the amendment, so the amended provisions cannot be identified from it.
independent_command_check: The order contains no appointment, committee, delegation, report direction or other command independent of the code. Its recital, which refers to the Board of Inquiry created by Executive Order No. 6840, states the reason for the amendment and commands nothing. The order ends with the President's signature, "The White House," and the date; it has no line recommending approval.
savings_check: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the Code of Fair Competition for the Cotton Textile Industry, as amended by this order, before June 14, 1935, and any fine, injunction or conviction already completed, are accrued effects that the repeal did not undo; the section 5 antitrust exemption for action already taken under an approved and effective code is likewise an accrued effect. The proviso to section 2 of the resolution names agreements and action thereunder and states no time limit, and the held text does not settle whether it narrowed that exemption for past action under codes. No held source continues the approval after June 14, 1935, and no held source shows a prosecution under this code continued after that date; nothing here continues the approval itself.
